subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me a 6-mark exam-style question on {lo} for {board} {level} {subject}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A cell is 0.05 mm wide. What is this in micrometres (µm)?
Which of these could cause a species to become extinct?
options: A new predator or disease and loss of habitat
questions.explain: New predators, disease, habitat destruction or environmental change can all drive a species to extinction.

questions.q: An image of a cell is 30 mm long and the magnification is ×1500. What is the actual size?
questions.explain: Actual = image ÷ magnification = 30 mm ÷ 1500 = 0.02 mm = 20 µm.

questions.q: What is the main function of the nucleus in a eukaryotic cell?
options: Controlling the cell and storing genetic material
Controlling what enters and leaves the cell
questions.explain: The nucleus contains the DNA and controls the cell's activities.

questions.q: What is the function of the cell wall in a plant cell?
options: Controls what enters and leaves the cell
questions.explain: The plant cell wall is made of cellulose and provides strength and support.

options: Humans choosing organisms with desired traits to breed together
Letting nature choose which organisms survive
questions.explain: In selective breeding humans choose parents with desirable characteristics to breed over many generations.

questions.q: A nerve cell (neurone) is long and has many branched connections. This adaptation allows it to:
options: Carry electrical impulses over long distances and connect to many cells
questions.explain: The length and branches let neurones transmit impulses across the body and link to many other cells.

questions.q: In the binomial naming system, an organism is named using its:
questions.explain: Binomial names use the genus (first, capitalised) and species (second), e.g. Homo sapiens.

questions.q: Which feature is present in a bacterial (prokaryotic) cell?
options: A single loop of DNA in the cytoplasm
questions.explain: Bacteria have no nucleus; their genetic material is a single circular DNA loop free in the cytoplasm, sometimes with plasmids.

questions.q: What is the function of ribosomes?
questions.explain: Ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis.

options: Breeding two organisms over many generations
Exposing organisms to sunlight to change genes
Transferring a gene from one organism into another
questions.explain: Genetic engineering transfers genes from one organism into another, e.g. inserting a human gene into bacteria.
